digest_markdown:
• A supply chain attack on SolarWinds' Orion IT monitoring system, used by over 30,000 organizations, allowed hackers to deliver backdoor malware in a software update, compromising approximately 18,000 customers [1].
• An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang, TeamPCP, and helped disrupt the group's attempts to exploit victims, allowing Google to monitor the hacking spree from the inside [2].
• CrowdSec's private GitHub repositories were compromised when an employee's account was used to copy code, exposing 83 CrowdSec users' email addresses and 51 potential investors' information [3].
• A GhostAction supply chain attack on GitHub repositories led to the theft of 3,325 secrets, exposing tokens and keys across widely used platforms, including PyPI, npm, DockerHub, and AWS [4].
• The GhostAction campaign compromised at least 817 repositories, with malicious commits deployed across different projects, affecting nine npm packages and 15 PyPI packages [4].
